::::{#exm-penalized-least-squares}
#### Penalizing the slope of a three-point fit

Take $n = 3$ observations with $x = (-1, 0, 1)$ and $y = (1, 0, 2)$,
the basis $b_0(x) = 1$, $b_1(x) = x$,
and a penalty on the slope only, $\mat{P} = \sbmat{0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1}$.
The pieces of @thm-penalized-least-squares are

$$
\ba
\tp{\mat{B}}\mat{B}
&= \sbmat{n & \sum x_i \\ \sum x_i & \sum x_i^2}
&& \text{(columns } 1 \text{ and } x\text{)}
\\ &= \sbmat{3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2}
&& \text{(} \textstyle\sum x_i = 0,\ \sum x_i^2 = 2\text{)}
\\ \tp{\mat{B}}\vy
&= \sbmat{\sum y_i \\ \sum x_i y_i}
&& \text{(columns } 1 \text{ and } x\text{)}
\\ &= \sbmat{3 \\ 1}
&& \text{(} 1 + 0 + 2 = 3,\ -1 + 0 + 2 = 1\text{)}
\ea
$$

so $\tp{\mat{B}}\mat{B} + \l\mat{P} = \sbmat{3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 + \l}$, which is diagonal, and

$$
\ba
\evb_\l
&= \sbmat{1/3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1/(2 + \l)} \sbmat{3 \\ 1}
&& \text{(invert the diagonal matrix)}
\\ &= \sbmat{1 \\ 1/(2 + \l)}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$

- With $\l = 0$, the slope is $1/2 = 0.5$: the ordinary least-squares slope.
- With $\l = 2$, the slope shrinks to $1/4 = 0.25$.
- As $\l \to \infty$, the slope shrinks to 0, and the fit is the constant $\bar{y} = 1$.

The intercept stays at 1 because the penalty does not involve it.
::::
